comment: Mac mini iOS HITL bench catalog — read by hitl-reserved --runner darwin on the Mac (nix/hitl-darwin.nix). Unlike the Linux benches there is NO container: the darwin runner grants each reservation a scoped SSH login into the shared daemon user, and the iPhone (devicectl/usbmux) and the C6 (esptool over /dev/cu.usbmodem*) are reached host-native from that session. So components carry NO 'devices' mounts (nothing to bind into a container); hardware is selected by env markers (a serial port, a UDID) instead. This host currently has ONE iPhone + ONE C6, so it offers a single real-iPhone unit (ios-phone); the ios-sim/second-C6 unit is dropped until a second C6 is attached. The port/serial/UDID below were filled against the live Mac (C6 MAC 8c:fd:49:12:56:e8 via esptool flash_id; iPhone UDID 00008110-000E5CE10251A01E). host/workspace + the unit sshd-port range are passed as flags by hitl-darwin.nix, not baked here.

components.comment: The real-iPhone unit's C6 DUT, reached host-native by esptool over its USB-serial port (macOS names it /dev/cu.usbmodem<N>). No 'devices' mount — the darwin runner has no container. HITL_ESP_PORT pins the port the toolbox targets; HITL_ADAPTER_SERIAL selects the board's USB-JTAG for any openocd/gdb use. macOS assigns the /dev/cu.usbmodem<N> number dynamically, so it can renumber across replug/reset — if flashing can't open the port, re-probe `ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*` and update HITL_ESP_PORT.
components.name: c6-c

components.comment: The iOS dev device: a real iPhone reached host-native via CoreDevice (devicectl) + usbmux — NOT a USB passthrough (the darwin runner has no container). Carries no device node, just the env markers: HITL_IOS_UDID selects this exact iPhone for devicectl build/install/launch (tools/ios_build_server.py); HITL_PHONE_TARGET routes phone_e2e to the iOS-device lane.
components.name: ios-dev

units.comment: REAL-iPHONE unit: the iPhone + its C6. The client reserves it (scoped SSH into the Mac daemon user), ships the phone-HITL harness + web bundle, and runs phone_e2e --phone-target ios-phone: builds/installs the Capacitor app on the real iPhone via devicectl (ios_build_server), opens it at ?driver=…&ble=real, and the PHONE provisions the real C6 over CoreBluetooth (Capacitor Improv plugin) → maps/solves end to end. Not pin_only: a bare `--require-caps ios-device,real-ble` request should match it.
units.name: ios-phone
